about: THE list of settings a person installing Hikari Index can set: one name and one default per setting, whichever way it is installed.

Every way of installing (compose.yaml, the second-machine compose files, any container template) offers these names with these defaults and no others. tests/settings/check.py holds the compose files, their .env examples and the programs' own reads to this file; its first lines say what it does not check.
The user docs' settings page (hikari-index-docs, content/reference/settings.md) is held to a copy of this file. Change a setting here, in the wrappers and there, in one sitting.

name: what the person types (a line in .env). compose_own: Compose reads it itself, so compose.yaml never names it. reads: which program gets it, under which name. routes: the ways of installing that offer it. names: where a route has released the same setting under another name, that name. only: the setting exists because of how that one route is packaged, and why.

The all-in-one image (containers/all-in-one) takes the settings whose routes include all-in-one, as variables on its one container; its start scripts hand each program its own and nothing else. What the compose install's first-run step makes, it makes itself on first start and keeps in its config folder. The analyze worker beside it is its own container and takes an analyze worker's settings, as on a second machine.

default_on: where a route cannot have the usual default, what it has instead; why_default says why. also_on: where a route takes the setting from one more place when its own name is unset, that place, and why. note_on: what else is true of the setting on that route.
Not in this list: compose.db.yaml (a developer's database) and what is fixed when an image is built (build arguments, a Dockerfile's ENV).

settings.name: HIKARI_VIDEO
settings.what: The folder your video is in, mounted read-only at /source in the worker that reads it.
settings.only: Compose is told the host folder in .env; anywhere else it is whatever is mounted at /source.

settings.name: HIKARI_ORIGIN
settings.why_default: Compose publishes the port itself and knows it; a single container does not know what address or port it was given, so it refuses to start without one.
settings.what: The address you open the gallery at; the sign-in form refuses any other.

settings.name: COMPOSE_PROFILES
settings.what: Which analyze worker runs on this machine: gpu, cpu, or empty for none.
settings.only: Compose starts the analyze worker from the same file; anywhere else it is its own container.

settings.name: HIKARI_GALLERY_PORT
settings.what: The port the gallery is published on.
settings.only: Port publishing belongs to whatever starts the container.

settings.name: HIKARI_GALLERY_BIND
settings.what: The address the gallery's port is published on.
settings.only: Port publishing belongs to whatever starts the container.

settings.name: HIKARI_DB_DATA
settings.what: A folder for the database instead of the Docker volume.
settings.only: Where a mount comes from belongs to whatever starts the container.

settings.name: HIKARI_BACKUPS
settings.what: A folder for the daily database dumps instead of the Docker volume.
settings.only: Where a mount comes from belongs to whatever starts the container.

settings.name: HIKARI_DATA
settings.what: A folder for the run records and frames instead of the Docker volume.
settings.only: Where a mount comes from belongs to whatever starts the container.

settings.name: HIKARI_IMAGES
settings.what: A folder for the web images instead of the Docker volume.
settings.only: Where a mount comes from belongs to whatever starts the container.

settings.name: HIKARI_SECRETS
settings.what: The folder holding the file shoko-api-key.
settings.only: Where a mount comes from belongs to whatever starts the container.

settings.name: HIKARI_SHOKO_BASE_URL
settings.what: Shoko's address. Without it, Shoko is off.

settings.name: HIKARI_SOURCE_ROOTS
settings.what: Names for folders inside the video mount, as name=/path pairs separated by commas.

settings.name: HIKARI_ANALYZE_STANDBY
settings.what: 1 makes the analyze worker a fallback: it takes a stage only when no regular analyze worker has checked in for ten minutes.

settings.name: HIKARI_WORKER_HOURS
settings.what: Start the worker's stages only between these hours, for example 01-07, on the clock HIKARI_TZ names. Empty means any time.

settings.name: HIKARI_TZ
settings.why_also: A host such as unRAID sets TZ on every container to its own time zone; the all-in-one uses that when HIKARI_TZ is not set, so its hours are the server's without anything typed.
settings.what: The time zone HIKARI_WORKER_HOURS and the times in the logs are in, for example America/New_York. Empty means UTC.

settings.name: HIKARI_POLL_SECONDS
settings.what: How often an idle worker asks for work, in seconds.

settings.name: HIKARI_ADMIN_LINK
settings.what: 0 hides the Admin link in the header. The link only; /admin still answers.

settings.name: HIKARI_NOTICE
settings.what: A line of your own text at the foot of every page.

settings.name: HIKARI_VERSION
settings.what: Which published images to run: latest, a release number, or dev.
settings.only: Compose builds the image names from it; anywhere else the version is the tag on the image name.

settings.name: HIKARI_DB_PASSWORD
settings.what: The database's password. The database is created with it.

settings.name: HIKARI_ADMIN_USER
settings.what: The admin sign-in name.

settings.name: HIKARI_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH
settings.what: A hash of the admin password.

settings.name: HIKARI_SESSION_SECRET
settings.what: Signs the sign-in cookie.

settings.name: HIKARI_ANALYZE_TOKEN
settings.what: The analyze worker's token, the other half of its pair in HIKARI_WORKER_TOKENS.

settings.name: HIKARI_WORKER_TOKENS

note_on.all-in-one: The container makes the pair of the analyze worker named analyze and adds it itself; the setting lists only other workers, and the container refuses to start if it names analyze.

settings.what: Every analyze worker's name:token pair, separated by commas.

settings.name: PUID
settings.what: The user id the programs run as and that owns the files they write.
settings.only: The compose install's images run as a fixed user, 10001; a single container on a host that owns its shares as another user (unRAID: 99) has to take that user's id.

settings.name: PGID
settings.what: That user's group id.

settings.name: HIKARI_GALLERY_URL
settings.what: The main machine's gallery, by address and port.
settings.only: On one machine the wrapper knows where the gallery is.

settings.name: HIKARI_WORKER_ID
settings.what: This worker's name on Jobs; it must match its pair in HIKARI_WORKER_TOKENS.
settings.only: On one machine the wrapper names the worker analyze.

settings.name: HIKARI_WORKER_VERSION
settings.what: GPU worker: the built image's tag and the version it reports.
settings.only: The GPU worker is built where it runs, never pulled.

settings.name: HIKARI_IMAGE_REPOSITORY
settings.what: CPU worker: pull from a registry of yours instead.
settings.only: Compose builds the image name from it.

settings.name: HIKARI_SHARE_VOLUME
settings.what: The Docker volume that holds the main machine's data share.
settings.only: Where a mount comes from belongs to whatever starts the container.

wiring.DATABASE_URL: Where the database is. The wrapper builds it from HIKARI_DB_PASSWORD and its own layout.
wiring.HIKARI_RUNS: Where the gallery finds the run records inside its container.
wiring.HIKARI_IMAGES: Where the web images are inside the container (not the .env line of the same name, which is the host folder).
wiring.HIKARI_OUTPUT: Where the worker writes run records inside its container.
wiring.HIKARI_SHARE: Where the analyze worker finds the run records inside its container.
wiring.HIKARI_SHOKO_API_KEY_FILE: Where the Shoko key file is inside the gallery's container.
wiring.HIKARI_DEVICE: cpu or cuda; decided by which analyze image runs.
wiring.HIKARI_GALLERY_VERSION: Set when the image is built.
wiring.HIKARI_WORKER_TOKEN_FILE: A file holding the analyze worker's token, read when HIKARI_WORKER_TOKEN is not set. The all-in-one writes one, and the analyze container beside it is pointed at it, so nothing is pasted between the two.
wiring.HIKARI_WORKER_VERSION: Set when the image is built (the GPU worker's compose file takes it from its settings file for that).
wiring.HIKARI_READ_ONLY: A switch in the gallery that turns it into a viewer. No way of installing offers it; a viewer is run from the gallery-readonly image.
wiring.HIKARI_WORKER_ID: For the worker that reads video: its own name, source. (For an analyze worker on a second machine it is a setting, above.)
wiring.PORT: The port the gallery listens on inside its container; set in the gallery image.
wiring.BODY_SIZE_LIMIT: The largest upload the gallery takes (an analyze worker's results); set in the gallery image.
wiring.OMP_NUM_THREADS: The text encoder's thread count, 4; set in its image and again in compose.yaml.
wiring.HF_HUB_OFFLINE: Keeps the text encoder from looking for its model online; set in its image and again in compose.yaml.
wiring.TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE: The same, for the other library that would look.
wiring.HIKARI_LIST_POLL_SECONDS: How often the worker looks for a folder to list. Internal; 5.
wiring.HIKARI_FFPROBE: A path inside the worker image.
wiring.HIKARI_PALETTE_BIN: A path inside the worker image.
wiring.HIKARI_RUN_STARTED: Set by the analyze stage for the steps it starts.
